articles.title: Even the Resident Evil Movie Isn't Safe from the PlayStation Physical Disc Controversy
articles.summary: If you thought the new Resident Evil movie trailer would be safe from the PlayStation physical disc controversy, think again.
articles.body:
If you thought the new Resident Evil movie trailer would be safe from the PlayStation physical disc controversy, think again.

The latest teaser video for director Zach Cregger's live-action Resident Evil adaptation was immediately flooded with negative comments published on the PlayStation YouTube channel yesterday. It's the latest example in the weeks of outrage that have followed Sony's decision to kill support for physical discs in 2028.

While most gamers have directed the backlash to gaming-related announcements, Resident Evil's status as a film doesn't seem to have deterred angry fans hoping to make their voices heard. Of the 1,800 comments left below the PlayStation upload for the trailer, most of the "Top" messages reference the controversy in one way or another. Some are more clever than others.

"I cannot wait to get the physical version of this," one fan, echoing the comments left on other PlayStation videos, said.

"He’s transporting the last physical game copy in existence," another joked.

"Leon…. Where are the Physical Discs?" someone else said.

PlayStation social media accounts have served as a hub for fans to voice their…feelings about Sony's physical strategy since the company made its initial announcement July 1, 2026. The move will see it cease production for new physical video games starting January 2028, meaning titles launched after the cutoff date will be completely restricted to a digital release. Players, especially those who have spent the last 50ish years collecting and trading physical versions of games , aren't happy, to say the least.

After a short social media hiatus, PlayStation returned to X/Twitter and was immediately swarmed by angry comments . Every post since then has faced a similar level of backlash, with the outrage spreading to other sites, too. The Marvel's Wolverine game is the latest example of a game trailer to be flooded by those calling for change .

It's not too surprising to see the PlayStation upload for the Resident Evil trailer filled with comments. While the vast majority of the backlash seems to have stuck to PlayStation channels, even other comment sections aren't free from references to physical game discs.

"I cant wait for the physical edition!" one viewer replied on the Sony Pictures version of the video .

The Resident Evil movie is only the latest to fall victim to the controversy, but it's not the first time it's found itself in the line of fire. Longtime fans were disappointed to see Cregger had taken some creative liberties when it comes to the Raccoon City Incident when they laid eyes on its first teaser in April, for example.

This looks so good but also pic.twitter.com/2KlEuvbGBS

Im hyped but 👇 pic.twitter.com/bvhRGY9DjK — SIDTYPE (@ghost42_00) July 23, 2026

The Weapons director will bring his Resident Evil to theaters September 18, 2026. For more, you can read about some of the Easter Eggs tucked into the new trailer . You can also read about how Sony may have been prepared for the backlash , and why it's unlikely to U-turn .

Corsair GALLEON 100 SD Stream Deck-Integrated Mechanical Keyboard

Corsair's keyboards are entirely gaming focused, and while the GALLEON 100 SD is also designed first and foremost for gaming, its unique feature-set offers endless potential for streamers as well. Amidst its numerous bells and whistles, the built-in Elgato Stream Deck is its crowning trump card. An Elgato Stream Deck is essentially a control pad with programmable keys, each with its very own display. Although it can serve myriad purposes, such as dedicated hotkeys for gamers or shortcut keys for multi-taskers, it has found a particular niche as a workflow tool for streamers.

The Stream Deck integrated into the GALLEON 100 SD consists of twelve customizable LCD keys, a 5" 720x1280 IPS color display, and two rotary knobs with multi-layer functionality. For a streaming gamer, these shortcut keys might be used to control games, switch to Discord or Spotify, access streaming tools, tweak system functions, and more. Corsair has even conveniently pre-installed ready-to-use profiles for some of the most popular streaming games including Helldivers, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Cyberpunk 2077, ARC Raiders, Resident Evil, and more.

Your gaming skills have to be top-notch if you're going to be showcasing your talent, and this keyboard won't hold you back on that front either. The GALLEON 100 SD is a full-sized keyboard (but with the Stream Deck replacing the traditional numpad) built into a solid aluminum frame. It boasts ultra-responsive 8,000Hz hyper-polling that virtually eliminates input lag and hot-swappable Corsair MLX Pulse linear mechanical switches. Linear switches are inherently on the quieter side since they're not clicky, but Corsair ups the ante with six layers of sound dampening foam. After all, you don't want your streaming audio to be punctuated by the clickety-clack of your keys. Other features include full key (NKRO) with 100% anti-ghosting, per-key RGB LED lighting, a magnetically attached cushioned wrist rest.

IGN's Will Judd recently had the opportunity to review this keyboard and gave it high marks. He pointed out that this keyboard is essentially one of a kind; no keyboard is more ideal for streamers and macro fiends to improve workflow. If you're not the target audience, there are more economical options. But if you are, only the best will suffice.

articles.title: Ridley Scott Reportedly Says Paul Mescal Wasn't ‘Masculine Enough’ for Gladiator 2
articles.summary: Director Ridley Scott reportedly blamed Paul Mescal for Gladiator 2's underperformance, claiming the lead actor wasn't “masculine enough” for the role.
articles.body:
Director Ridley Scott reportedly blamed Paul Mescal for Gladiator II 's underperformance, claiming the lead actor wasn't “masculine enough” for the role.

According to Puck News’ Matt Belloni (via World of Reel ), this was the real reason why Mescal dropped out of Scott’s next film, The Dog Stars , and was replaced by Jacob Elordi.

Reports at the time claimed Mescal’s exit from The Dog Stars stemmed from scheduling conflicts with Sam Mendes’ four-part Beatles movie, where Mescal plays Paul McCartney .

IGN’s Tom Jorgensen, for one, appreciated Mescal’s performance, writing in his positive Gladiator II review that “Paul Mescal is adept in the belabored-hero role, going toe-to-toe with not only the delightfully deranged Joseph Quinn and Fred Hechinger, but also with Denzel Washington.”

While Gladiator II earned $462 million worldwide, the long-awaited sequel to the 2000 Best Picture winner also cost anywhere from $250 million to north of $300 million to produce.

The Dog Stars is one of the biggest box office flops of Ridley Scott’s career , opening to just $19 million worldwide on what was reportedly an $89 million budget.

In other Ridley Scott shit-talking news, the director recently said he’s developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant with Michael Fassbender because he thinks the Fede Alvarez-directed Alien: Romulus was just “OK” and the franchise “needs some help.”

Also be sure to read IGN’s picks for Ridley Scott’s 10 best movies, a list that doesn’t include Gladiator II, The Dog Stars, or Alien: Covenant.

articles.title: Ever Wanted to Sleep Inside a Giant Pokéball? In Japan, You'll Soon Have a Chance
articles.summary: What is it actually like inside a Pokéball? In Japan, you'll soon be able to find out.
articles.body:
One of the biggest questions I've always had about Pokémon (and I have quite a few) is this: what is it actually like inside a Pokéball?

If memory serves correctly, the Pokémon anime series has occasionally shown a Pokéball's interior, with a miniaturized creature lounging inside. But I've always wondered how comfortable this is, and what if a Pokémon is claustrophobic? And why aren't there any windows?

Despite all of this, if someone told me I could go experience what living inside a Pokéball was like, I'd still likely take them up on the offer. And this is why I'm particularly intrigued by an upcoming collaboration between nap-tracking app Pokémon Sleep and the luxury Japanese hospitality firm Not a Hotel.

In a nutshell: you will be able to sleep inside a Pokéball soon.

このモンスターボール、本当に泊まれます。 ◤￣￣￣￣￣ 『Pokémon Sleep』✖️ NOT A HOTEL #泊まれるモンスターボール 宿泊キャンペーン開催決定！ ＿＿＿＿＿◢ 詳細は9月15日（火）公開💤 #ポケモンスリープ pic.twitter.com/habKvYosxT

A trailer for the experience reveals a giant spherical pod shaped like a half-open Pokéball, with its floor space largely taken up by a generous-sized spherical bed. And, yes, there is a window — though no curtains that I can see.

If you're intrigued to roleplay as a Pokémon and clamber inside a giant ball, then you'll want to keep an eye on the upcoming lottery (of course there's a lottery) on September 15 to secure your spot. You'll also need to travel to Hokkaido, Japan, where the Pokéball pod will be located, so do bear that in mind.

Prefer your bed without a giant perspex window, and also in your own house? That's fine too. And you'll have plenty of Pokéballs to throw in the next major entries in the Pokémon series, with Pokémon Winds and Waves on the way next year.

articles.title: New Street Fighter Trailer Teases Conflict Between Ryu and Ken, and E. Honda Does His Hundred Hand Slap
articles.summary: Legendary has dropped a new trailer for the Street Fighter movie showing E. Honda pulling off some of his iconic moves and teasing some unexpected tension between Ryu and Ken.
articles.body:
Legendary has dropped a new trailer for the Street Fighter movie showing E. Honda pulling off some of his iconic moves and teasing some unexpected tension between Ryu and Ken.

Street Fighter is hurricane kicking its way to theaters on October 16, and a new trailer has been shown in the lead-up to its release that features some of the game’s core cast members throwing down in familiar locales.

One of the more notable fighters who got some time to shine in this trailer was E. Honda, who we see facing off against Ryu in his famous bath house stage. He pulls off his Sumo Headbutt move (and surprisingly, it doesn’t look totally absurd), as well as his Hundred Hand Slap. For a moment, it looks like Ryu is on the losing end of this fight before he sends Honda flying with a Tatsumaki.

We also get to see Ryu and Ken brawling in a dark alleyway, and it seems like these two have had a falling out at some point, likely spurred by Ryu dropping off the face of the earth to pursue a path that appears to involve the Dark Hadou. We see him charging up a purple fireball as he says there was “darkness growing” within him — while Ken tries and fails to release a single Hadouken in his swanky apartment.

“I spent years living in Ryu’s shadow,” Ken says, promising to “win it all” at the World Warrior tournament thrown by M. Bison, who secretly plans on stealing the strongest fighters’ powers for himself (or something to that effect).

Chun-Li informs Ryu that Ken is in danger and urges him to "fight" and save him, though we aren’t sure of the specifics just yet. Could this be a parallel to the animated 1994 movie, where Bison captures Ken, brainwashing and transforming him into Violent Ken?

Cody Rhodes also gets some time to shine as Guile, who, in this movie, is a sarcastic, smart-mouthed guy as opposed to his stoic in-game counterpart. He delivers a few funny lines, one of which sees him interacting with Andrew Schulz’s Dan Hibiki.

Notably, Roman Reigns also makes an appearance as Akuma, lifting up Alexander Volkanovski’s Joe with the power of the Satsui no Hadou.

All in all, there’s a lot to chew on and break down in this trailer. Multiple characters are shown in various shots throughout the nearly three-minute-long clip, including Vega (Orville Peck), Balrog (50 Cent), Cammy (Mel Jarnson), and many more.

Street Fighter: Cast Revealed for Legendary's Live-Action Movie

Street Fighter hits theaters on October 16. For more news on this adaptation of Capcom’s iconic fighting game series, check out our interview with David Dastmalchian at San Diego Comic-Con, where he told us all about how he dove deep into the minds of historic cult leaders to bring M. Bison and Shadaloo to life.

articles.title: Rockstar Games Reveals Its Official GTA Online Roleplaying Server, nopixel V
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has revealed its official GTA Online roleplaying server, nopixel V, ahead of GTA 6's launch.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games has revealed its official GTA Online roleplaying server, nopixel V, ahead of GTA 6's launch.

Grand Theft Auto 5 is one of the most popular games of all time, and part of that is thanks to major community support. In the late 2010s and early 2020s, modders went particularly crazy with the foundation Rockstar created and utilized it for roleplaying servers, such as the extremely popular nopixel. Rockstar has embraced this side of the community, acquiring the team behind the FiveM modding platform and collaborating with nopixel itself.

Now, nopixel is gearing up to release the next iteration of its roleplaying server, which will be officially supported by Rockstar Games. The two teamed up to produce a much richer and deeper roleplaying experience that will feature a reworked character customization system, enhanced graphics, and a wealth of quality of life changes. Perhaps the most notable thing for longtime GTA fans is that the Mile High Club, a building that has been under construction since the game's very first reveal trailer in 2011, has been finished exclusively for nopixel. The building is now a hotel and casino for roleplayers.

The server will be available directly through Rockstar's official launcher, meaning you won't have to tinker with any third-party tools or platforms, and players will be able to see it in action on September 8 when a bunch of the top RP streamers will be let loose on the streets of Los Santos. You can click here to check out a trailer , which showcases the depth and uniqueness of this new GTA experience.

Of course, many fans are likely going to wonder what this means for GTA 6. Rockstar Games has yet to make any kind of comments or announcement on the next iteration of GTA Online, but it would be shocking if there wasn't an online mode for GTA 6 later down the line. The single-player of GTA 6 is already a very roleplay-intensive experience , so it seems like Rockstar may be designing the game with a roleplay future in mind.

Whether nopixel will have its own GTA 6 RP server remains to be seen, but it would be surprising if Rockstar abandoned this side of the game when entering the next era. If this is just the beginning of a long term collaboration, GTA 6's online could be extremely special.

articles.title: Wolverine, Control Resonant, and 4 More Big September Games We've Already Played and Can Tell You About
articles.summary: September is here, which means the Fall is here, which means some of the biggest games of the year drop this month. We've already played some of the biggest ones, so check out our previews of Marvel's Wolverine, Control Resonant, and more on this page.
articles.body:
September is here, which means the Fall is here, which means some of the biggest games of the year drop this month . We've already played some of the biggest ones, so check out our previews of Marvel's Wolverine, Control Resonant, and more below.

If Insomniac has proved anything over the last eight years, it’s that they know how to make a hell of a superhero game. Spider-Man remains one of the PlayStation 4’s defining action games and a shining example of open-world design, as are both of its follow-ups. Now they’re looking to replicate that magic with Wolverine, albeit this time as a traditional linear AAA action game. I got to play about two and half hours at a recent preview event, and while my impressions are mostly glowingly positive, I did come away with a few questions and concerns. Read our full Marvel's Wolverine preview .

I stepped into my exclusive two-hour-long demo of Control Resonant hoping to see more of what I love so much about Remedy’s output — unrivalled world-building, consistently surprising level design, and simply being shown things I haven’t seen before. Thankfully, I was not disappointed. Read our full Control Resonant preview .

After seven years, Fire Emblem is finally returning to the world introduced in Fire Emblem: Three Houses. There’s a lot of similarities to be found in the structure of Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, but there are also plenty of ways that developer Intelligent Systems is building out the features that defined Three Houses in some pretty exciting ways. Even though I was only able to get just a few chapters in with each of the main heroes, I’ve already found several new additions I’m very fond of… and maybe one that I’m not as high on. Read our full Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave preview .

There's always a foggy town that instills a certain fear, cryptic puzzles within that tense atmosphere, and an underlying trauma to ground the chilling horror. I had an inkling that Silent Hill: Townfall could nail the series' particular style of horror, and after getting three hours of hands-on time with it, I'm thrilled to say my intuition was spot on. This being in first-person definitely sparked the thought of what P.T. could have been, because my time with Townfall showed that the more intimate interaction with the environment can bring you closer to both the story it's trying to tell and the gameplay elements that give rise to such dread. I came in thinking Townfall would be just another direction the series could explore, and came away eager for whatever comes after the end of my preview demo. Read our full Silent Hill: Townfall preview .

From my 30 minutes of hands-on time, I really came to appreciate the sense of freedom of taking my chosen vehicles out into the field. The Burnout Paradise-style open-world racing is a great fit for the toy-car world of Hot Wheels, as the focus on exploration offers a surprisingly charming space to tear my way through. Hot Wheels: Infinite Rush is very much a living toy box of a world to unravel, and so far, developer Milestone has got a great concept for its big upgrade for Hot Wheels racing games. Read our full Hot Wheels: Infinite Rush preview .

Effectively capturing the vibes of Garfield can be a real challenge to pull off well, but Garfield: Escape from Monday is shaping up to be a worthy addition to the lovable slacker’s library of interactive adventures. Much like the recent Bubsy 4D, Escape from Monday is pretty familiar when it comes to the structure and formula, but that’s seemingly by design, as recapturing the fun of 3D platformers from a simpler time is very much in style these days. Luckily, his new Garfield adventure backs up solid fundamentals with snappy platforming action and a cool hook that showcases the endearing sourpuss in a fun and exciting way. It might not reinvent the genre, but that’s okay, and as Garfield will tell you any day of the week, there’s nothing wrong with a little comfort food. As long as it’s not healthy vegetable lasagna on a Monday morning. Read our full Garfield: Escape from Monday preview .

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: LEGO Lord of the Rings Minas Tirith Set Is Now Available at Amazon
articles.summary: After being backordered on the LEGO Store for months, LEGO Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith is finally available and shipping at Amazon.
articles.body:
Heads up, Tolkien fans: the biggest Lord of the Rings set LEGO has ever made is now available at Amazon . Previously a LEGO Store exclusive (where it’s been backordered for months), this massive city-scope build is now available at the internet’s preferred retailer. It still costs $649.99, but it also still comes with 8,278 pieces, making it one of the biggest LEGO sets ever, regardless of category.

It took a long time to piece together, but LEGO expert Kevin Wong built this set for IGN and wrote about the experience , awarding it “our highest recommendation.”

What’s so great about LEGO Minas Tirith, the capital of Gondor? For starters, it’s just straight-up impressive as a physical object. It’s a gorgeous white walled city, intricately detailed, that works as a decoration for whatever room you display it in. It’s big and impressive, despite that it’s made on a scale small enough to depict the entire city all in one set.

LEGO The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith

While the front of the set is micro-scale, the back of Minas Tirith depicts some of the city’s interiors in minifigure scale. One smaller room contains a Palantir that lets the owner see things happening far away. But the main room is the Hall of Kings, complete with the throne for the King of Gondor.

I know I’ve been tossing around words like “micro” and “mini,” but make no mistake, this is a huge set. Just look at the dimensions of the finished product above – it's roughly two feet tall and two feet wide. It comes in a giant box that contains about 60 bags of LEGO pieces. All told, it has over 8,000 pieces, meaning piecing it together is a marathon, not a sprint. But when you’re done, you’ll have a gorgeous piece of Lord of the Rings you can put on display for the rest of your life (as long as you don’t drop it).

For more, check out our full rundown of every LEGO set out in September , as well as our mega-list of release dates for every upcoming LEGO set .

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass September 2026 Wave 1 Lineup Announced
articles.summary: Microsoft has announced the Xbox Game Pass September 2027 Wave 1 lineup, and it includes a Call of Duty blockbuster.
articles.body:
Microsoft has announced the Xbox Game Pass September 2026 Wave 1 lineup, and it includes a Call of Duty blockbuster.

Available today on all major Game Pass tiers, Shelldiver is an incremental game about a senior turtle trying to start a business selling jellyfish. It sounds odd, but its Steam reviews look promising, so maybe this is one worth hauling in.

Later this week, Speedrunners 2: King of Speed launches straight into Game Pass, bringing a second helping of competitive co-op platforming action. Game Pass premium members also gain access to Dice a Million, the roguelike deck builder already on other tiers.

Perhaps this batch's biggest inclusion is Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, which is the Raven Software-made instalment that arrived back in 2020. We gave the game's single-player a 7/10 in our campaign review , though its multiplayer modes lagged behind that a little. There have been better CODs, in other words, though there have also been worse.

Later this month sees the addition of The Royal Writ, another roguelike deck builder, though this time with a medieval twist. Then there's Virtua Fighter 5, or Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage, to give its full name. "The World Stage" refers to its single-player "journey," though its bone-shattering multiplayer modes remain the star.

Last but not least, there's the previously-confirmed inclusion of Runescape: Dragonwilds , the first standalone title in Jagex’s long-running medieval MMORPG franchise. Dragonwilds has already shifted over 1 million copies during early access, so its open world, co-op, crafting and survival gameplay is obviously doing something right.

Shelldiver (Cloud, Console, and PC) — September 1, Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

articles.body:
This year's Labor Day sales have officially begun and the first solid LEGO deal of the week has arrived. The 3-in-1 Haunted Mansion set has dropped to it's lowest price ever on Amazon, now 20% off.

If you've been looking for a cool LEGO set to build this Halloween, this discount is absolutely worth a look. As a 3-in-1 set, this Haunted Mansion can also be converted into a Haunted Train or a Haunted ship.

LEGO's Creator line produces some of my favorite sets because of just how versatile these builds are. Right out of the box you can choose to go in three different directions, and each build includes instructions. Seeing as this set is marketed as a Haunted Mansion, that is likely the only build that will use all 736 pieces.

If you do buy this set and only have one specific build in mind, I suggest you start with that one first. I built the 3-in-1 Medieval Horse Knight Castle last year and found it a bit challenging to convert it to a different set once I put together the first one. It's certainly possible, but the instructions for each version of the set include which bag to open next, so once all of the bags are open you're stuck with a big pile of bricks rather than being able to sort everything one bag at a time.

As for what you get with this Haunted Mansion set, it's actually quite a bit for the price. It comes with five minifigures in total, including a skeleton, a ghost, Frankenstein, a vampire, and a werewolf holding a bone club. All of these classic Halloween monsters work best with the Haunted Mansion set, but I'm definitely partial to the Haunted Train build . They even gave the skeleton a little conductor hat just for this version of the set so he can feel official.

There's a Newer Haunted Mansion Set Out Now

It's a new month, which means there are a bunch of new LEGO sets releasing in September . One such set is the new LEGO Icons Mayor Manor. This is a much larger 18+ build that is a major upgrade over the smaller 3-in-1 set. It's already on backorder at the LEGO Store, but you can also find it available on Amazon .

If you like the idea of a spooky mansion you can display on your shelf, Mayor Manor is the better option. It's the first of LEGO's new Midnight Valley Collection and utilizes asymmetrical elements and tilted angles to achieve higher levels of spook than ever before.

articles.title: Sony Rolls Out New Customer Harassment Policy After Physical Disc Controversy Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: Sony Japan has introduced a new customer harassment policy following widespread backlash toward its decision to stop producing physical game discs starting January 2028.
articles.body:
Sony Japan has introduced a new customer harassment policy following widespread backlash toward its decision to stop producing physical game discs starting January 2028.

Sony Japan published this policy on its official website on September 1, 2026, where it outlined several examples of harassment and urged customers to honor its behavioral guidelines.

“Our company strives to provide honest service so that our customers can use our products and services with peace of mind, and we value customer feedback to improve our services,” it wrote. “On the other hand, the dignity and safety of our employees must not be threatened by customer harassment, such as words or demands from customers that exceed what is considered reasonable according to social norms.”

Sony went on to say that it takes a “firm stance” against such behavior, which includes examples like “persistent and repeated, or prolonged, demands, excessive or unreasonable demands for compensation or apologies, and abusive language, threats, slander, and other similar behaviors.”

Other examples included “forcing someone to prostrate themselves” and “visiting our offices or related facilities without permission.” If any such behavior is confirmed, Sony says it may “restrict or suspend customer service” to protect its employees — and, if necessary, contact “police, lawyers, etc.” to take legal action or begin criminal proceedings against them.

Sony is one of several Japanese companies implementing such measures to protect their employees. In October 2025, a new law was enacted that required employers across the country to take action to prevent harassment toward their workers by customers. As told by Uni Global Union , this marked a massive shift in Japan's workplace culture, pivoting from a “customer is always right” mentality to a focus on worker protections.

Sony's policy hasn’t come out of the blue; the company has borne the brunt of backlash from angry players following its decision to stop making physical game discs, along with its divisive response to an ongoing lawsuit as a result of this strategy.

In August, Sony responded to a class action lawsuit that accused it of failing to clearly state that players are merely purchasing a revocable license when they buy a game on its digital store, arguing that “in the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining ‘ownership’ of a digital game.”

A Dutch consumer group and the Stop Killing Games movement have also banded together to sue Sony, alleging that the company charged Dutch customers more on its digital store than buyers located elsewhere in the world.

The PlayStation store is at the center of another lawsuit against Sony in Mexico, where lawmakers argue that the company is engaging in “anti-competitive practices” by limiting purchases to its digital storefront, crippling competition from other games retailers.

Sony, for its part, is continuing to pursue an all-digital future, with chief financial officer Lin Tao saying it will "cautiously move this forward" with its plan to kill off game discs despite “strong views” from players.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Orbitals Is a Co-op Sci-fi Adventure That Looks and Feels Exactly Like a Playable '90s Anime, One Any Toonami Fan Should Be Excited For
articles.summary: A co-op adventure that nails the feeling of a playable ‘90s anime.
articles.body:
Orbitals sets out to carve its own space in the co-op-only genre. This bold adventure takes the joyous camaraderie of split-screen puzzle solving and couples it with a striking throwback anime visual style that captured my attention from the very first frame. The actual puzzling never reaches for new or daring ideas in the same way, mostly content to emulate its contemporaries with familiar concepts rather than push the limits of what's possible in cooperative games, which can make it a bit predictable at times. But exploring the unknown bounds of space with a partner is still an endearing romp that was well worth the 10 hours it took to reach the end.

Orbitals is solely a two-player experience, but thankfully it has both local and online play, as well as a friend pass that allows you to give someone else a copy that's only playable with the original owner; similar to what developer Hazelight does for games like It Takes Two and Split Fiction. This flexibility is good because everything in Orbitals is designed for two people, and the coordination many puzzles require is further emphasized by the fact that you're able to see your partner's side of the screen at all times, regardless of whether you play locally or online.

It makes a stunning first impression before you even get to that action, with a stylized player select menu that takes all of the charm of the early 90's anime you would see on Toonami and distills it into a nostalgia that felt tangible. Instantly, I was transported back to those late nights staying up past my bedtime in my parent's wood panelled basement to catch an episode of Cowboy Bebop or The 08th MS Team; a portal into a world I wouldn't come to fully understand until much later in life.

Orbitals thrives in its ability to evoke that era of animation, and attempts to push it one step further by thrusting you into the roles of two protagonists with fitting archetypes – Maki, a disorganized and somewhat blindly optimistic hero, and Omura, a slightly more put together and calculated counterpart. Together, they often feel like two sides of the same quirky and curious coin. These two often bounced off of each other; when Maki's high energy and over-the-top enthusiasm would start to take over, Omura would come in and rationalize a situation or further assess the problem. It brought a necessary balance to the dynamic, keeping everything in line.

After their ship colony was nearly decimated by a powerful storm in space, both Maki and Omura were put into an I.M. – a machine that will reprint their bodies and keep their thoughts, emotions, and memories intact. Orbitals lightly touches on themes of what it means to be reprinted, with Omura making asides about if this is really him anymore after so many reprints, sometimes poking at these ideas philosophically but never fully wrestling with them. I wanted more from these ideas, especially as they come back around toward the end of Orbital's story, but they were never given time to fully flesh out that framework.

Tasked by your leader Togen to collect Cassettes that power your colony's ship, you'll venture out into the expanse. My partner and I started to delegate responsibilities as soon as we left our primary colony and headed for our travel ship. I helmed the main gun for the majority of our playthrough, blasting away any enemy ships or rockets that came within spitting distance. My partner in crime took the reigns of the ship itself, and he deftly drifted us through dangerous corridors, dashed out of the way of incoming attacks, and sometimes got us lost to the point where we struggled to make our way back on track.

The ship is the primary way of getting to your next objective. Orbitals is not an open world game, but it offers small pockets of freedom to fly around in. You'll fly to different rifts in the wall surrounding your colony to explore outside the bounds of charted territory. When you land in a new location, you're treated to big, bold text across the screen like you've loaded up the next episode in your VHS. You'll grab the highlighted weaponry from the center of the ship and head outside to a clearly marked hatch, and these hatches are where you find the more traditional action-adventure-style levels.

Early on, my partner and I explored a large mining operation run by robots with a knack for rhythm, which forced us to move to the beat as we looked for a Cassette in the deepest depths of mine shafts. We would pound in time with large drums, hop across moving platforms that swung side to side to the groove, and even found some form of alien life screaming along with the tune. These engaging moments mixed the world of Orbitals into the puzzle designs, making each puzzle feel contextually interesting and relevant as they fit with that rhythmic theme.

Most puzzles put the focus on a few different weapons that are introduced early on. Rather than constantly reinventing the wheel in each new level, Orbitals teaches you the primary ways you will interact with the world around you and then puts smart twists on those fundamentals throughout. Each zone will often require two different gadgets that are stashed on your ship – these range from a laser beam that powers robots and guides drones to a grappling gun used to open panels and rotate platforms. My partner and I often took turns swapping between this simple yet effective arsenal of puzzle-solving tools, constantly trying to guess who would have the more interesting job once we reached a level and who would be relegated to moving platforms for the other person.

We solved a myriad of puzzles as we bounced from sector to sector – some were great, demanding teamwork or making us feel clever for having figured them out, while others felt more like we just stumbled into the answer rather than discerning a satisfying solution. More than once we were left scratching our heads wondering why something had worked, which speaks to a general lack of visual feedback. While many interactable objects are clearly marked with identifiable imagery, it's not always intuitive what Orbitals wants you to do with those pieces.

Some puzzles are as straightforward as having someone hook a yellow lever to pull down platforms for the other to jump and dash across, providing a simple yet effective way across chasm or dangerous terrain. Other puzzles are a bit more involved, such as trying to get a small platform around tight corners by simultaneously shifting your weight left and right while also using the grapple to slingshot yourself and get around even tighter turns.

Challenges like that are where Orbitals really shines – the tandem nature of these hurdles forced us to tighten up our communication even if we both thought we were Pacific Rim drift compatible. It required focus as we swirled around this seemingly never-ending maze of twists and turns, but once we locked in and got our methods airtight, we overcame the obstacle and improved our communication skills in the process.

Introducing all of its base weapons upfront means you're exposed to fewer new mechanics as you get deeper in. As a consequence, Orbitals struggles to do anything transformative or with a final flourish toward the end. Two-thirds of the way through, I felt I had seen all of the tricks it had to offer, and an overeliance on its ship sections began to wear on me. While there were a few small surprises here and there, I spent the last three or so hours mostly going through the motions as I waited to see how it would wrap up. For how short of a game Orbitals is, it feels like it stumbles across the finish line with its final few sequences rather than taking a triumphant victory lap.

Despite that weak third act, Orbitals does a lot to make up for it in its smaller moments. As we walked around the ship interior in-between zones, it was fun to discover all of the new life that had stowed away. Capybaras, weird hi-fiving robots, and more began to breathe personality into our little vessel, making each journey to a new area exciting and filled with wonder as we waited to see who would choose to make this place their own next.

This cold hunk of steel went from nothing more than a means of transportation to a comfy and cozy home. As we explored more regions, we opened up new rooms onboard and found mini-games to compete in, complete with leaderboard spots to fight over. These rooms brightened up the space with ship combat simulators, electric jump ropes, and the kinds of diversions that made this world full of whimsy and intrigue.

The ship also contains smaller details that flesh out Omura and Maki as more well-rounded characters. Stumbling into Maki's disheveled and disorganized room with a drum set in the corner perfectly contrasts Omura's immaculately kept bedroom with a piano. The way they put their arms up when running down staircases, or how they interact with the many objects around the ship – these details inject personality into these characters outside of the main conversations and cutscenes. There is a curiosity throughout Orbitals, everything begging to be poked and prodded with an inquisitive nature.

Its story emulates some of the great plots of early 90's anime, but does little to rise above its inspirations or put its own stamp on these tales. Its early hours focus on the pressure put on Maki and Omura to travel beyond the broken colony, searching for machinery to keep their dwindling colony from extinctiown. It vaguely gestures at a larger conflict brewing, alluding to a dangerous storm approaching or differing ideologies on what it means to truly be alive, but it waits too long to meaningfully grapple with its more existential and interesting threads. I wanted to see more punch from a game so clearly inspired by a murderer's row of the great anime that came before it.

Despite its cooperative nature, this world can feel very isolating. You venture out into the great unknown and are sometimes met with deafening silence. Maki and Omura acknowledge that this silence could spell the end of their way of life, but rarely does Orbitals bring the stakes to match such a powerful concept. Instead, its main story hook relies heavily on gathering magical macguffins so Togen can put his plan into action. It doesn’t dwell on its self-reflective moments or give them room to breathe, swiftly ushering us from one level to the next with little reflection or examination as to how they all connect. It really is a story centered on Maki and Omura providing for their colony, and hoping to make everyone's lives better in the process – and while that’s enough to carry it across the finish line, it does fall short of the full potential it clearly has.

Whether we were on the ship or exploring an asteroid, all of Orbitals is carried by an eclectic soundtrack from artists like Swedish music duo Falk and Klou and Japanese singer-songwriter Mami Ayukawa. Its songs strike a balance between paying homage to anime of the 80's and 90's while finding its way to stand on its own. This soundtrack elevates everything around it without feeling like a backdrop just to set the scene – and the use of dynamic music that changes as you explore each zone gave them distinct personalities. It’s another tool in developer Shapefarm's belt to bring the vision of playable anime to life, and perhaps its most effective.

articles.title: Peter Cullen’s Final Optimus Prime Performance Confirmed for New Transformers Short
articles.summary: The late Peter Cullen's final voice performance as Optimus Prime will debut in a new animated short alongside select 40th anniversary Transformers: The Movie screenings.
articles.body:
The late Peter Cullen ’s final vocal performance as Optimus Prime will be in a new animated short film, Optimus Prime: Awakening, that will be presented following select 40th anniversary screenings of The Transformers: The Movie .

Hasbro and Fathom Entertainment announced the short film Tuesday:

“Optimus Prime: Awakening is a fully realized, 12-minute animated short designed as a love letter to the Transformers community and the late Peter Cullen, the legendary talent and voice of Optimus Prime. Optimus Prime: Awakening builds on the acclaimed storytelling and visuals of The Transformers: The Movie (1986), giving audiences the rare opportunity to experience the iconic cultural moment from the franchise’s past while exploring its future on the big screen.”

Hasbro and Fathom said, “Peter’s performance [in Optimus Prime: Awakening] reveals a deeper vulnerability while retaining the unmistakable strength and authority that made his portrayal iconic.”

Check out the key art for Optimus Prime: Awakening below.

Frank Welker, who voices Optimus Prime’s archenemy Megatron in the film, praised his late co-star in a statement:

“Optimus Prime and Megatron were made for each other. After all, one needs the perfect hero against the epitome of evil to create great drama. Peter’s portrayal of Prime was born of his own personal beliefs; honesty, loyalty, and always insisting on doing the right thing. This made it easy to be friends. Returning as Megatron and Soundwave for one final story opposite Peter’s Optimus in Optimus Prime: Awakening was a real gift. I will miss my friend, but that voice and his heart and values will always be part of Optimus Prime.”

Peter Cullen died August 26 at the age of 85.

The Transformers: The Movie returns to theatres internationally in 4K from September 17–22, 2026. Fathom has just announced new screenings in France, Singapore, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama and Peru.

Fans can also now pre-order The Transformers: The Movie 40th Anniversary Limited-Edition steelbook , which will be available on November 17 in both 4K UHD and Blu-ray.

The streamer notes that, "Netflix counts a 'view' as one full-runtime equivalent of watch time. Netflix defines a view as the total hours viewed for a title divided by its runtime. So one household watching a 27-minute video twice looks the same in Netflix's math as two households each watching it once." They no doubt mention this since YouTube counts a view the moment a video starts to play, and so far, on Rockstar's official YouTube channel , the GTA 6 Extended Look has 17 million views as of 12pm PT when this story published.

articles.title: Resident Evil 2 Director Hideki Kamiya Says Capcom Has Grown 'Numb' to How Scary New RE Games Are
articles.summary: Hideki Kamiya has confirmed that he was “not joking” when he begged Capcom to make a less-scary version of Resident Evil Requiem for the faint of heart, even arguing that the company has become "numb" to how frightening the newer games have gotten.
articles.body:
Hideki Kamiya has confirmed that he was “not joking” when he begged Capcom to make a less-scary version of Resident Evil Requiem for the faint of heart, even arguing that the company has become "numb" to how frightening the newer games have gotten.

In March 2026, Clovers Inc. — Kamiya’s newest game development studio — uploaded a video showing the team playing Resident Evil Requiem . Kamiya stood off to the side as one of his employees got to a cutscene near the beginning of the game, where he complained that, “I've been saying for forever, they should make a 'non-scary' mode.”

He said as much in a tweet around that same time, suggesting an alternate mode where “the zombies get all cute, the blood splatters turn into cherry blossom petals, the music becomes this upbeat, feel-good kind of tune, and you can just purely enjoy the puzzles and battles in a fun mood.”

We’re all playing Resident Evil Requiem! Kamiya—who hates horror games—is doing his usual grumbling 🤭🍀 pic.twitter.com/ocbW8tsnDR — CLOVERS Inc. (@CLOVERS_en) March 10, 2026

We’re all playing Resident Evil Requiem! Kamiya—who hates horror games—is doing his usual grumbling 🤭🍀 pic.twitter.com/ocbW8tsnDR

Kamiya doubled down on this request in an August interview with Video Games Chronicle , saying he was “100% serious” about it and even claimed that Capcom is going too far with how scary its Resident Evil games have gotten lately.

“Nowadays, with how photorealistic and high-fidelity video games have gotten, the amount of crazy, horrifying things that people are able to put on the screen is absolutely insane, and I think anybody who’s on the Resident Evil teams at Capcom, at this point, they must all be completely numb to how scary the thing they’re making is,” he told the outlet.

“This is not a joke; I’m being one hundred percent serious when I say that I wish they would make it so that their games can also be enjoyed by people like me, who can’t handle scary games at all.”

Kamiya said he wanted to revisit the Raccoon City Police Department in Requiem to see how Capcom handled the iconic area that he first created in the original Resident Evil 2 — but it was just too scary for him.

“I mean, just recently this year we had Resident Evil Requiem and the big return of Leon Kennedy, and he went back to Raccoon City, and he’s reliving all of those memories and all of those experiences. As somebody who directed that original game, Resident Evil 2, I was curious to know how that panned out for him. I wanted to experience that myself as a player, but the game was way too scary, and I couldn’t,” he said.

He went on to state that he’s requested changes to how scary the RE games are directly to the series’ developers and producers — usually to stunned reactions.

“And so, it’s not a joke. I legitimately wished it would include some kind of non-horror mode for people like me, because I talk to folks who are on the Resident Evil teams at Capcom just privately, and I tell them that their games are way too scary, and they’re like, ‘What? Come on, they’re not that scary.’ They seriously seem to have no awareness of how scary the things they make actually are, so I really hope they address that at some point.

“I mean, it doesn’t even have to be anything super elaborate. You could just make it so that the zombies’ faces aren’t so scary. Why not have a mode that just puts, like, brown paper bags on all of their heads, or instead of having these dark, dingy rooms everywhere, they could have really pleasant mood lighting. I think even just making a few tweaks like those, it would make it so that somebody like me could make it all the way through the games. Oh, and no blood!

“Which is precisely why I don’t think the teams at Capcom fully understand how scary the games that they’re making actually are! I told [series producer] Takeuchi-san to his face, ‘Your games are too scary!’ And he was like, ‘What? Seriously?!’ I get codes for every new Resident Evil when it comes out and it always comes with an email saying, ‘Hey, we hope you enjoy the game!’ And I’ll send back an email thanking them for the code, and say, ‘Well, I’d love to play the game, but unfortunately it’s too scary for me, so I’m not going to be able to,’ they come back with, ‘Oh, come on, it’s not that scary, you can do it!’”

Kamiya even joked that he’d make a spin-off game where Leon finally gets to enjoy a peaceful retirement, where players would take him “fishing in the countryside, foraging for wild veggies, baking bread, walking the dog,” etc.

Unfortunately for him, it doesn’t look like Capcom is going to take his notes into consideration, as a remake of Code Veronica and all its terrifying zombie combat is set to release next year.

articles.title: Gruv Is Having a Massive DVD Sale on Classic Cartoon Collections
articles.body:
Gruv, one of the best places to buy DVDs, Blu-rays, and 4Ks , just launched a massive sale on classic cartoon collections. It shouldn’t come as a surprise that the bulk of the options are limited to DVD and Blu-ray — these are classics, after all. But with streaming services like HBO Max dropping cartoons like flies , any of these legendary animated shows are a worthy addition to your physical media collection.

Gruv Launches Legends of Animation DVD Sale

Gruv isn’t actually listing the original prices of the cartoon collections, so I’m comparing their prices to the listings currently available on Amazon. There’s also no clear end date for the sale, which at the very least will run through Labor Day weekend sales .

Given the Warner Bros. connection, it’s not a surprise that the sale includes a ridiculous amount of Looney Tunes. The cartoon squad is particularly topical with Coyote vs. Acme, the once-shelved Warner Bros. movie we recently gave a 9/10 review , now actually showing in theaters.

Having first aired in 1930, the Looney Tunes is a particularly long-running series that would be near-impossible to pack into a single DVD release. As such, Gruv is giving you tons of options. We’re talking the full lineup of collected seasons from across eras and anniversaries, as well as a decent chunk of film collections.

Looney Tunes: Bugs Bunny Anniversary Collection

Sabrina the Teenage Witch: The Complete Series

One of the best deals in sale is actually on a particularly recent release, at least in DVD form. The Tom & Jerry Golden Era Collection dropped last December , collecting 114 episodes of the original cartoon that aired primarily from 1940 to 1958. The $20 price drop on Gruv bring the box set to a lower price than it's ever been on Amazon .

Other discounted box sets include What’s New Scooby Doo, Sabrina the Teenage Witch, and a particularly great combo, The Flintstones and The Jetstons.

Gruv is an official storefront backed by Universal and Warner Bros, so it’s basically as close as you can get to getting these DVDs directly from the source. I’ve been covering Blu-ray deals for several years now, and quickly picked up on the fact that DVD discounts at retailers like Amazon are often just price-matching what was already happening directly at Gruv.

Like many things, it remains to be seen what exactly will happen with these physical media distribution deals and storefronts if Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. , which is currently on pause , goes into full effect.

articles.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Adds Noah Jupe to Highly Secretive Cast
articles.summary: Avengers: Secret Wars has added Noah Jupe to its cast in an undisclosed role.
articles.body:
Avengers: Secret Wars has added Noah Jupe to its cast in an undisclosed role.

According to Deadline , Jupe has been tapped to join the cast of one of the biggest movies on the horizon ahead of a shoot date later this year. The role is expected to play a "key part" in the story of the film. Absolutely no details were provided on who he's playing, but that doesn't mean we can't speculate, right? The most immediate guess is he's part of the new X-Men cast. Marvel announced a bunch of members of the next X-Men film at D23 , which includes Sadie Sink, Adam Driver, Kit Connor, Inde Navarrette, and a handful of other up-and-coming stars.

Jupe is 21 years old, which means he would fit in quite well with the other X-Men cast members. He also starred alongside Sadie Sink in a stage version of Romeo and Juliet earlier this year. However, there are a lot of questions over whether the new X-Men will even be in Secret Wars. If Jupe isn't part of the X-Men, he could be a character like Nova, who is getting his own standalone film in the future . It's anyone's guess right now, and given that Marvel tried to keep Sadie Sink's role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day under wraps up until release, we may not know until the film comes to theaters in December 2027.

Noah Jupe has made a name for himself with the Quiet Place franchise , Hamnet , and a number of other high-profile projects. He's the first person to be formally cast in Secret Wars, as we're not sure who will survive Avengers: Doomsday and appear in the sequel. It seems like a safe bet to imagine Robert Downey Jr. will return as Doctor Doom and the likes of Chris Hemsworth and Chris Evans will return as Thor and Captain America respectively, but beyond that, it's hard to say. Evans has already teased a "brutal" story for Cap in Doomsday , but it's unclear what that looks like at the moment.

Avengers: Infinity War killed half of its cast, meaning most of the characters didn't return until the third act of Endgame. It wouldn't be surprising if the returning X-Men cast from the Fox-era films are killed off in Doomsday, but Marvel will likely keep all of this under wraps until it releases. Either way, the Marvel universe appears to be expanding in exciting ways.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Says The Batman Part 2's Fight Scenes Are 'Significantly Harder' to Perform
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson says his age is making it harder to perform the fight scenes in The Batman Part 2.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson says his age is making it harder to perform the fight scenes in The Batman Part 2 .

The actor spoke with GQ ahead of the release of his new movie, Primetime, and naturally was asked about returning to the role of Batman. Pattinson noted that although the experience has been good and he's excited about the film, he's having a 'significantly harder' time with the fight scenes due to the large gap between movies.

“I’m definitely feeling my age when fighting a lot," said Pattinson. "I’m literally like, ‘Goddamn, this is significantly harder than it used to be.’ But it’s really fun. And I think the movie’s going to be pretty great. It’s got a really, really fun cast, but it’s a marathon.”

Pattinson was cast as Batman in 2019, when he was 33 years old. He shot the film throughout 2020 and 2021, meaning it's been roughly five years since he last put on the cape and cowl. Ironically, part of the conceit of Pattinson's take on Batman was that he'd be a younger and more inexperienced version of the reluctant hero. However, the long wait for a sequel means Pattinson is older than Christian Bale was in The Dark Knight Rises and just three years younger than Ben Affleck was in Batman v Superman. Those two takes on the character were meant to be older and more broken down versions of the character.

It has been a long journey to get cameras rolling on The Batman Part 2, but things finally came together earlier this summer. The film will boast an incredibly impressive cast with the likes of Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, and Brian Tyree Henry all being tapped for a variety of roles, though they're largely being kept under wraps. A variety of set photos and videos have been popping up on social media for the last few months, showing intense action scenes in a snow-covered Gotham City .

The Batman Part 2 has had a variety of release dates over the years and was originally meant to release in October 2027 when production began. Unfortunately, the team behind the film opted to push it to a February 2028 release , so it will be a while before we see the Caped Crusader back on the big screen.

articles.title: Christopher Judge Physically Prepared to Play Kratos in Live Action God of War Series But Backed Down For This Reason
articles.summary: Christopher Judge revealed that he actually started physically preparing to play Kratos in Prime Video’s live-action God of War series before he made himself back down.
articles.body:
Christopher Judge revealed that he actually started physically preparing to play Kratos in Prime Video’s live-action God of War series before he made himself back down.

Speaking on a panel at Fan Expo Canada, Judge said he began working out to get in Spartan shape and started memorizing his lines, admitting that he’d been in talks to take the role in the project’s early days.

"We had talked, and I thought, 'God, what a great legacy to leave for my grandson.' So I started working out. I got bigger,” he began.

“Then, just the reality of it... because I did read! I did read for it. It was so hard for me to memorize my lines, which I never had a problem with. And that was my mind and body starting to tell me, 'You don't want to do this.' I was one of the leads of Stargate at 33 to 44, and then stopped. Now, at 62, to be the lead, I just have no desire to live that way again."

As noted by Collider , Judge previously mentioned the physical toll that such a part would have taken on him. “I didn't want to do it," he said. “I didn't want to, at 62 years old, work 16-to-18-hour days. I didn't want to be dieting constantly; I didn't want to be working out constantly."

That being said, Judge is more than happy for Dave Bautista to take the part , though he is concerned about the pro wrestler-turned-actor getting shredded again after losing so much weight in recent years. He also shared his reaction to Ryan Hurst initially getting cast for the role, saying he felt the actor was a perfect choice due to his history with the God of War games.

“With Ryan, I thought that was absolutely the right choice. He's played all the games. He's a gamer and new father; like, who better? Then when he got hurt, it was like, are they going to take time to read with and call people back? So when I heard the name of Bautista, I thought, 'Didn't he just lose like 100 pounds?' So I hope he's going to be great. I think he's going to be great. I just hope it doesn't cause any health issues to put back on all that weight,” he said.

Prime Video’s God of War series suffered a major setback in July when Hurst tore his bicep filming a stunt for the show. Rather than wait out his lengthy recovery, Amazon decided to recast the role to Dave Bautista in one of the best castings we’ve ever seen for a game adaptation.

While fans balked at the first look we got at the show back in February, responses are looking more positive now that this news has been revealed, alongside a newer photo that Hurst shared of himself in full Kratos makeup that looked far better than the initial poster.

Judge previously criticized Prime Video's God of War series back in August, slamming showrunners for not involving the writers of the 2018 game it's based on (though, in this panel, he clarified that he wants "anything God of War to be great").

articles.title: On first listen, the Sonos Beam Ultra sounds great
articles.summary: We tested the Sonos Beam Ultra, the new $699 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos soundbar launching September 29th.
articles.body: Sonos unveiled a bunch of new stuff today at its open house event. There’s the $699 Beam Ultra soundbar and the $449 Ace Ultra headphones, plus several under-the-hood app updates (some coming sooner than others). While the show floor was a less than ideal venue to judge audio quality of either new product, a private demo in a smaller room provided a better hint as to what the Beam Ultra soundbar might be capable of. With the 7.1.2 soundbar about six feet in front of the press, the team ran through a couple demos to show off its range, particularly with Dolby Atmos content. The opening minutes of Widow’s Bay subtly illustrates the Beam Ultra’s enhanced bass, improved vocal clarity and Atmos chops. There are a lot of small details that didn’t get lost in the mix, like walkie talkie chatter, extraneous sound effects that build the world, plus the eerie swelling of the score to amp suspense. There’s only so much sound that can come out of such a relatively small soundbar, but I was impressed — both at how it sounded and how Sonos found the ideal room to bounce around the sound coming from its side- and top-firing drivers. [Image: The Beam Ultra looks similar to the older Beams, except it has holes poked on its top for its upward-firing speakers to fire through. Sonos then wirelessly paired two Play portable speakers to the Beam Ultra, then set them behind us as rear channels for a demo with Sinners (the electrifying “I Lied To You” scene). If you have a small-ish living room and don’t want to permanently mount rear satellites, this setup might suffice for you. It’s certainly loud enough. Pairing more speakers seemed to let the Beam Ultra focus more on delivering a balanced, full sound with better directional audio than its predecessor, the Beam Gen 2, which virtualizes its spatial audio effect (as in, it fakes it) due to lacking side- and upward-firing speakers. My colleague John Higgins will spend a lot more time with the Beam Ultra in an upcoming review. My first impression was good, but that’s how press events usually go. You’re using these products with a pro at the wheel, and sometimes in more ideal circumstances than our homes allow. As someone who bought a Vizio Elevate SE system last year, I was surprised by how punchy the Beam Ultra sounded during the demos. Sometimes, it sounded a little too good, and the presence of Sonos subwoofers and extra speakers in the demo room was tough to ignore, despite the team assuring us they weren’t used. Nevertheless, I’m curious how it holds up in a home environment, and specifically how it sounds across a range of content when it’s the only Sonos speaker you have. Sitting between the $499 (currently $399) Sonos Beam Gen 2 and the $1,099 (currently $899) Sonos Arc Ultra, the Beam Ultra splits the difference between the two in terms of hardware features. You’ll get a proper taste of Atmos content without spending close to $1,000, and without straying outside of the Sonos ecosystem. The Beam Ultra launches September 29th, and preorders are available now at Best Buy, B&H Photo, Sonos, and Amazon. Photography by Cameron Faulkner / The Verge

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Proves Unreal 5 Can Be Done Well
articles.summary: Just like with Star Wars Zero Company and Halo: Campaign Evolved, The Blood of Dawnwalker runs on Unreal Engine 5, and has been shockingly free of technical problems. The game doesn't have the same issues with crashing and stuttering that Zero Company has, and scales down a lot better than Halo: Campaign Evolved does, although I would still avoid running it on something like a handheld gaming PC.
articles.body:
I've been playing a lot of The Blood of Dawnwalker over the last week or so, and while the game does successfully stress out my gaming PC, I've been surprised at just how stable it is.

Just like with Star Wars Zero Company and Halo: Campaign Evolved , The Blood of Dawnwalker runs on Unreal Engine 5, and has been shockingly free of technical problems. The game doesn't have the same issues with crashing and stuttering that Zero Company has, and scales down a lot better than Halo: Campaign Evolved does, although I would still avoid running it on something like a handheld gaming PC.

I've been primarily playing The Blood of Dawnwalker on an admittedly powerful system with an AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D , 32GB of RAM and an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 – well above its recommended specs. And the game pushes even this system, only delivering around 70–80 fps most of the time at 4K with the Ultra preset and DLSS set to Quality.

While I'd love the frame rate to be even higher, the problem I've had with a lot of Unreal 5 games is the constant stuttering. I still haven't finished the Silent Hill 2 or Metal Gear Solid 3 remakes that came out last year, even though I love those games, primarily because they can become a stuttery mess at times, especially when loading into a new scene. The Blood of Dawnwalker, however, has remained stable at all times.

The Blood of Dawnwalker - Prologue Screenshots

It's not limited to my main PC, either. I have the Steam Machine set up on my TV, and while I do have to lower the PC settings dramatically, I can get 55–60 fps at 1440p with mostly medium settings and the game looks just fine. And even on the Steam Machine, which has a much weaker CPU and less memory, I still don't get the kind of stuttering and crashes that Unreal 5 has become known for on weaker hardware.

I've even had a chance to play the game a bit on the PS5 and Xbox Series X , and The Blood of Dawnwalker runs like a dream on those consoles too. The visuals do scale down quite a bit on those consoles, but it feels good to play. I haven't had the chance to grab capture to run through a frame rate analysis tool, but the game feels like its running at around 60 fps on the PS5 Pro, and at least 40-50 on the Xbox Series X, with the Performance profile and the Balanced profile, respectively.

But while the game does run smoothly on the consoles, Dawnwalker is one of the few Unreal games where I'd recommend anyone with a decent rig to play it on PC instead. It's a beautiful game, especially once you get out into the wilderness, and the console versions lose quite a bit of detail and foliage density.

This is the type of game where I'd expect a bit of jankiness, too. I've played a ton of niche RPGs that run like garbage, like the Gothic Remake , but I stick to regardless because of their depth. Thankfully, the Blood of Dawnwalker avoids that entirely, despite running on probably the most annoying game engine on the market right now, and that's incredible.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra
